pass_a_gloss: Having willed that you learn the precision of the things proposed by you to us, my beloved brother Theophile, I considered it reasonable, having drawn abundantly as from a holy spring from the divine scriptures themselves, to place before your eyes the things being sought, so that you may not only be gladdened by the hearing of these things with the ears, but also, having been empowered and having understood the matters themselves, you may be able to glorify God in every way. For this is to be a provision for you in the present life without danger from us, so that you, having brought forth from prepared words the things difficult to know and hard to grasp for many, may sow them in the breadth of your heart as in fertile and pure land, and you may despise those who contradict and speak against the saving word. But be afraid lest these things be entrusted to unbelieving and blaspheming tongues, for the danger is not random, but rather entrust them to pious and faithful men who wish to live holily and righteously with fear. For not in vain did the blessed apostle, writing to Timothy, command, 'Keep the deposit, turning away from profane and empty speeches and contradictions of the falsely named knowledge, which some, promising about the faith, have missed the mark.' And again, 'You, therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus, and the things you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men, who will be sufficient to teach others.' And so the blessed apostle, with caution, handed over these things, which are not for all, foreseeing in the Spirit that the faith of all is in danger, how much more will we be in danger if we simply and as it happens hand over the words of God to unholy and unworthy men?

pass_b_english: Because you wanted to learn the precise details of the topics you proposed to us, my beloved brother Theophilus, I judged it right to set before your eyes exactly what you asked for, drawing abundantly from the divine Scriptures as from a holy spring. My aim was that you would not only rejoice in hearing these things with your ears, but that, empowered and having grasped the realities themselves, you might glorify God in every way.

This present life calls for a safeguard from us, so that you may take what is difficult for many to know and hard to grasp, bring it forth from prepared words, and sow it in the breadth of your heart as in fertile and pure soil. You will then be able to despise those who contradict and speak against the saving word. But you must also fear lest these things be entrusted to unbelieving and blaspheming tongues; the danger is not a trivial one. Rather, entrust them to devout and faithful men who desire to live devoutly and righteously in the fear of God.

The blessed apostle did not command Timothy in vain when he wrote, 'Guard the deposit, turning away from profane empty talk and the contradictions of so-called knowledge, which some, by professing it, have swerved from the faith' (2 Timothy 1:13-14). And again he said, 'You then, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus, and what you have heard from me through many witnesses entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others also' (2 Timothy 2:2).

So the blessed apostle handed these things over with caution, because they are not for everyone. He foresaw by the Spirit that the faith of all is in danger. How much more, then, will we be in danger if we hand over the words of God simply and carelessly to unholy and unworthy men?
